name: Patient
sub: Books tests or home collection, pays, and gets reports with past trends on the phone.
steps: Gets tests ordered by the doctor or books a package
Books a home collection slot if wanted
Pays online or at the counter
Gives the sample; sees the time it was taken
Gets an SMS if the sample must be taken again
Gets the report link on WhatsApp
Sees trends of past results
Shares the report with any doctor or ABHA
cannot: See reports before the pathologist releases them
Get sensitive results (for example HIV) by SMS
notify: Sample due or home visit ETA

name: Doctor
sub: Orders tests with the reason, gets results in one inbox and is phoned for critical values.
steps: Orders tests or an order set with priority
Adds clinical notes for the lab
Sees status from ordered to released
Gets a call and an alert for critical values
Reviews and acknowledges results
Sees trends and delta flags
Adds a test to the same sample if stable
Discusses an unexpected result with the pathologist
can: Order, cancel before collection, add on tests
cannot: See a result before release (except critical calls)

name: Ward nurse
sub: Collects ward samples on the collection round and receives critical calls.
steps: Sees the collection list by time
Prints barcode labels at the bedside
Scans wristband and label, collects
Sends samples by porter or tube
Recollects rejected samples
Takes critical calls and reads back
Tells the doctor at once

name: Home collection phlebotomist
sub: Collects at the patient's home with the phone app, keeps the cold chain and hands over to the lab.
steps: Sees the day's route on the phone
Patient gets an ETA when the visit starts
Checks ID; prints or sticks barcode labels
Collects; takes payment by UPI or cash
Logs cool-box temperature
Hands over at the lab within 4 hours
Reception scans and accepts the bag
cannot: Accept cash above the legal limit

name: Lab reception and collection
sub: The front door of the lab: walk-in collection, sample receipt, rejection and send-outs.
steps: Registers walk-ins; checks payment
Collects at the counter
Receives ward and home samples by scan
Checks label, tube, volume, time
Accepts or rejects with reason
Packs send-out tests for the partner lab
Gives printed reports to walk-ins

name: Lab technician
sub: Runs QC, analysers and manual tests, enters results and phones critical values.
steps: Runs QC at the start of each run
Starts the run only if QC is in control
Gets results from analysers; enters manual ones
Checks flags, delta and critical alerts
Phones critical values; logs read-back
Technically verifies the results
Sets up cultures and reads plates
Stores samples for the retention time
can: Enter results and verify them technically
Run QC and reject a run
cannot: Run patients when QC is out of control

name: Pathologist
sub: Validates and releases reports, reports histopathology and owns the lab's quality.
steps: Reviews held results (delta, critical, flags)
Validates and releases with comments
Reports histopathology and cytology
Signs culture and sensitivity reports
Reviews QC and EQAS results
Amends a released report with reason when needed
Talks to doctors about unexpected results
cannot: Release own technician entries without review (two-step rule)

name: Lab in-charge
sub: Sets up tests, ranges, critical limits, analysers, send-out labs and watches TAT and quality.
steps: Maintains test master and reference ranges
Sets critical limits and delta rules
Sets Westgard rules per analyser
Approves partner labs for send-outs
Watches TAT, rejections and workload
Runs NABL quality indicators monthly
Plans reagents with the store
can: Edit lab masters (price changes need approval)
cannot: Change prices without Super Admin approval
Delete a test with history (retire only)

name: Management
sub: Watches lab volume, revenue, TAT, quality and send-out cost.
steps: Volume and revenue by test and department
TAT and critical-call compliance
Rejections by ward
Send-out share and cost
QC and EQAS status
Approves new tests and price changes
notify: TAT below target for a week
